intelligence.human_view: This supersedes the 01:49Z assignment in his own live word: it was unfold for About and slideshow for Skills — one format each — and now it is BOTH formats for BOTH pages. About gets the unfold down and the slideshow; Skills gets the unfold down and the slideshow; a bridge page offers the choice (in a nutshell, then "which presentation do you want?"). The one shared data source feeds all four presentations — one source, four faces, no copies drifting apart. And in the same breath he re-emphasized the two laws the formats live or die by: motion must never falsely imply that work is happening (Design Law #4 — the unfold must never pretend to be working when it is only moving), and color is a language, not decoration (Design Law #5 — every color in the formats means something). The formats are the presentation; the laws are what make the presentation honest. And the timing matters: the amendment went to the Personal coordinator BEFORE its build step, so the round builds both formats from the start instead of building one and redoing it — the correction landed before the work, not after it. This is the correction compound working as designed: the lesson lands in the same hour as the build it governs.
intelligence.simple_view: About and Skills BOTH get BOTH ways to look at them — the unfold-down way AND the slideshow way! And remember: moving must never pretend to be working, and every color must MEAN something!
